name: timidity
why: A software synthesizer that renders MIDI through General MIDI soundfonts, a classic instrument you can drive from the terminal.

brief.what_it_is: TiMidity++ is a software synthesizer that plays MIDI files by converting them into PCM waveform data. It takes MIDI files plus digital instrument data (Gravis Ultrasound compatible patch files and/or SoundFonts) and synthesizes them in real time, playing the result. It can also save the generated waveform to disk as audio files such as .wav, .au, .aiff and .ogg. The homepage lists ncurses, GTK and Win32 GUI interfaces, and says it understands SMF, MOD, RCP/R36/G18/G36 and MFI files.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to play MIDI files without any external MIDI instruments at all. It is also a continuation of TiMidity 0.2i by Tuukka Toivonen, released in 1995 and no longer developed, which Masanao Izumo and others carried on as TiMidity++; the ++ marks the difference from the original.
brief.how_it_works: The synthesizer reads MIDI data and combines it with instrument voice data (GUS-compatible patches or SoundFonts) to generate PCM waveforms in real time, which are sent to the audio output. The same generated waveform can instead be written to a file in one of several audio formats. The page also mentions remote MIDI playback over the network, playing MIDI from inside archive files, a spectrogram display, and trace playing.

brief.install_notes: Release 2.13.0 is on SourceForge's release page and mirrors; the news also lists 2.13.1, 2.13.2 and 2.13.3 tarballs (2.13.3 only fixes a Win32 compile error). Packages exist for FreeBSD, NetBSD, many Linux distributions, Mac OS, and Windows or Cygwin. To build from source, the page says it uses GNU autotools and should be easy if you have gcc. For an unreleased build, you can use hourly source tarballs or the CVS repository. You also need instrument data: Gravis Ultrasound patch files and/or SoundFonts, which the project does not bundle according to the page.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, free-software MIDI synthesizer that renders General MIDI sound entirely in software, so it needs no hardware synth. It can also write rendered audio to files in many formats, not just play it.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage's newest news item is dated 2004-10-04 (the 2.13.3 release), and the footer says Copyright 2003. I did not check any other repository or release page, so I cannot confirm whether later versions exist.
brief.caveats: The homepage is an old 2004-era site, and its download and CVS instructions may be stale: the page says CVS was moved by SourceForge. Development sources are explicitly unstable. The page does not mention a license version beyond GNU General Public License. Building from source is documented only briefly, and the page is thin on usage (no command-line examples for playing a file). Installing instrument data is up to you. The homepage was reachable.
quotes: TiMidity++ is a software synthesizer. It can play MIDI files by converting them into PCM waveform data.
It can not only play sounds, but also can save the generated waveforms into hard disks as various audio file formats.
TiMidity++ is a free software, distributed under the terms of GNU general public license.
TiMidity++ uses GNU's autotools, so compiling it may be easy.
